answer: Admission needs 2 peers to post a counter-bond equal to the newcomer's own, so the cost of entry is carried by parties with something to lose. Since the sable escrow holds both sides, recruiting real counterparties is the operator's cost, and the ledge audit releases each pair. A farm running 72 keys cannot self-supply these, because each counter-bonding peer must be independent on the nadir graph and each one exposes its own stake to the same slash. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
